Hunted for evidence mass fraud is small, costly per attempt, or not financially motivated; IC3 reports 859,532 complaints and over $16B in losses in 2024. It does not measure “cheap” or “scalable.”
Mass-market fraud is cheap, scalable and financially motivated.

Mass-market fraud is large-scale and financially motivated: 859,532 IC3 complaints and over $16B in reported losses in 2024. “Cheap” and “scalable” are analytical characterizations, not measured here.
Strand case study; Threadlinqs TL-2026-4197; Action Fraud A-Z

Hunted for a source supporting the full hotel vector list (payment data, PMS, locks, third-party IT); Strand supports Booking extranet/guest-data concentration, Threadlinqs title supports booking impersonation, Action Fraud A-Z returned 403. AIMI and Ingram Toft excluded per instruction.
Hotels combine transient guests, shared networks, payment data, property-management systems, electronic locks and third-party IT contractors; documented incidents show that concentration.
Documented hotel/booking-account cases show concentration of guest data and third-party access; the assigned sources support booking-account phishing, not the full PMS/payment/lock vector set.
Assigned sources support only part of the compound claim.
Amnesty International, Pegasus forensic methodology report

Hunted for evidence Pegasus was indiscriminate or mass-deployed; Amnesty documents targeting of human-rights defenders and journalists across countries, not a population-scale deployment. No denominator supports “smaller than the fear.”
The commercial spyware market is targeted and smaller than the fear.
Commercial spyware is targeted at human-rights defenders, journalists and civil-society figures; “smaller than the fear” is an analytical judgment, not a measured comparison.
Would refute if Kaspersky described only generic malware. Source confirms hotel-network compromise, executive targets, fake updates and 2007–2014 activity.

Hunted for evidence MGM was a Wi-Fi exploit or that no settlement occurred; CISA confirms help-desk social engineering; NLR confirms a $45M settlement. The ~$100M impact was not in the fetched CISA/NLR sources.
The 2023 MGM intrusion began with a help-desk vishing call, not a Wi-Fi exploit; MGM reported roughly US$100 million in impact and later a US$45 million settlement.

The 2023 MGM intrusion began with help-desk social engineering, not a Wi-Fi exploit; CISA confirms the help-desk vector, NLR confirms a $45M settlement, and MGM’s 8-K is the basis for the ~$100M figure (not in the fetched CISA/NLR sources).
Help-desk vector and $45M settlement confirmed; $100M source not fetched.
Would refute if counts/properties differed. Source confirms 3M+ doors, 13,000+ properties, 131 countries, forged keycards, no known exploitation.

Hunted for the 42-charge/January-2025 claim; found a May 2024 charging release with nine counts and a December 2025 sentencing report saying the man pleaded guilty. “42” is the man’s age, not the charge count.
The AFP charged a man in 2024 for running fake "free airport Wi-Fi" networks that harvested email and social-media credentials; he pleaded guilty to 42 charges in January 2025.
The AFP charged a 42-year-old man in May 2024; he pleaded guilty and was sentenced in 2025; reports list nine counts, and 42 is his age.
The charge count and plea date are wrong.
Action Fraud / North West Fraud Forum
Would refute if messages were not sent through platform messaging. Alert says in-app, email and WhatsApp messages from taken-over hotel accounts.

A guest network exposes MAC address, destinations, DNS queries and TLS SNI; timing/volume are plausible but not established by the cited source.
Would refute if the counts/date window differed. Source confirms 40+ organizations, 13 countries, activity from January 2017 through Q1 2019.

Android notifications: Notification listener harvests OTPs and message previews.
Notification access can read posted notifications; whether an OTP or message preview is exposed depends on the app’s notification content and redaction.
API capability confirmed; specific harvest not guaranteed.

A linked device can sync messages, approve logins or access files.
A linked device can sync messages; approval-of-logins and file access are not established by the fetched page.
Only the message-sync element is supported.
Apple Advanced Data Protection / iCloud security
Hunted for evidence all photo storage modes are equivalent; Apple documents E2EE categories and exclusions, not the full five-mode list.

A photograph can be local-only, synced to a cloud account, in an E2EE cloud service, in an encrypted local backup, or in a provider-keyed backup; the answer to “can someone access it?” differs for each.
Photo storage depends on sync/backup/encryption settings; the five categories are illustrative, not exhaustive.
Categories supported in part; list is illustrative.
Hunted for evidence account takeover is the single most common route; sources document common routes, not a ranked “most common” statistic.
Account takeover is the most common route to cloud content: phishing, reverse-proxy session theft, SIM swap, MFA fatigue or a reused password.
Account takeover is a common route to cloud content through phishing, reverse-proxy theft, SIM swap, MFA fatigue or reused passwords; “most common” is not established by the cited sources.
Microsoft Entra ID, Protect against consent phishing
Hunted for evidence consent phishing cannot reach mail/files; Microsoft documents permissions to cloud services/data. Mail/files access depends on the scopes requested, not all consent phishing.
OAuth consent phishing grants a malicious app API access to mail or files; the consent screen is real, but the app is not.
OAuth consent phishing grants a malicious app the scopes the user approves; mail or file access depends on the requested scopes, and the consent screen is hosted by a legitimate provider.

Hunted for evidence broad extension permissions cannot read page/session data; Chrome permissions support that capability. The Cyberhaven case confirms a malicious auto-update, not the exact all-site/cookie claim.

A browser extension with permission to read and change data on all sites can read pages, sessions, cookies and web-app content; a compromised developer account can push a malicious update to thousands of users.

Broad extension permissions can read page and session data; the Cyberhaven case confirms a compromised admin account pushed a malicious auto-update to users. The exact all-site/cookie scope is permission-dependent.
Capability and update confirmed; exact scope qualified.
Hunted for evidence the 6.9M figure is wrong; reporting confirms 6.9M profiles. The source fetch was blocked (HTTP 405), so the sharing-feature mechanism is reported but not directly verified.
The 2023 23andMe breach spread from a small set of phished accounts to 6.9 million profiles through the platform’s sharing features.
23andMe reported 6.9 million profiles affected after credential-based access; the sharing-feature spread is reported but the cited source was inaccessible.
Count supported by reporting; mechanism not directly verified.
Hunted for a single Marriott count; found 339M (FTC 2024), 383M (Marriott 2019) and 500M (early estimate) across different dates/scopes.
The corpus contains two Marriott/Starwood figures: 383 million (R15, R02) and up to 500 million (R36, R05); 500 million was an earlier estimate and 383 million a later disclosed figure.
The corpus contains three Marriott/Starwood figures: 339 million (FTC 2024), 383 million (Marriott 2019) and 500 million (early estimate).
A third count (339M) is present; the figures differ by date/scope.

Apple photo metadata / personal safety guide

Hunted for evidence photos cannot carry location metadata; Apple documents location metadata in Photos. The claim that email/cloud links “often do not” strip it is channel-dependent and not directly established.
Photos carry EXIF metadata including time, device and often GPS coordinates; messaging apps and social platforms may strip some, but email attachments and cloud links often do not.
Photos can carry EXIF time, device and GPS metadata; whether it survives depends on the sharing channel and its stripping behavior.
Hunted for the exact cloud-suite session-cookie chain; the Cyberhaven case stole Facebook access tokens, not this cloud productivity chain. The claim is illustrative, not a documented incident.

In the illustrative extension chain, a malicious extension update reads the session cookie for a cloud productivity suite and sends it to an attacker, who opens the account without a password or MFA prompt.
Illustrative only: a malicious extension update could read a session token and enable account access; the cited Cyberhaven case stole Facebook tokens, not this cloud-suite chain.
Hunted for per-user key derivation in WPA2-Personal; found a shared PSK/4-way handshake model. The exact “every user derives the same master key” wording is narrower than the fetched source.

In WPA2-Personal, every user derives the same master key from the same passphrase, so any guest given the passphrase can capture another device's handshake and attempt offline recovery if the passphrase is weak.
In WPA2-Personal, users share a passphrase/PSK; the 4-way handshake derives session keys, so a weak shared passphrase enables offline guessing if a handshake is captured.
Mechanism is shared PSK + per-session keys, not a single master key for all users.

Hunted for default management-frame protection in WPA2; found 802.11w is optional and WPA3 adds MFP. The claim’s “not protected by default” is directionally right but needs the optional-802.11w qualification.

WPA2 management frames are not cryptographically protected by default, enabling deauthentication and evil-twin tricks; WPA3-SAE with management-frame protection addresses parts of this only if both access point and client support it.
WPA2 management-frame protection is optional (802.11w), not default; WPA3-SAE/MFP addresses it only when both access point and client support it.

In 2025 WhatsApp attributed a spyware campaign to Paragon Solutions and notified affected users; the IFJ documented Italian journalists among those targeted, but the delivery mechanism and full target list were not public.

Hunted for evidence common symptoms are reliable indicators; MVT documents forensic analysis, not symptom-based diagnosis.
A missed call from an unknown number, battery drain, a disappearing notification or a strange message are not reliable spyware indicators; forensic examination (e.g. MVT) is needed for a real signal.
Common symptoms are not sufficient indicators; forensic examination (e.g. MVT) is needed for a real signal.
Symptom list not established by MVT; framing narrowed.
Hunted for evidence the cited sources document a messaging implant reading decrypted content; they document zero-click exploitation, not the endpoint-decryption chain.
In the illustrative messaging chain, an implant reads encrypted conversations after decryption on the endpoint; encryption is not broken in transit.
Illustrative only: an implant that has compromised the endpoint can read messages after decryption; encryption is not broken in transit.

The WhatsApp server routes ciphertext and does not hold content keys, but it processes account information, phone number, device information, connection information and usage data in order to deliver messages.
WhatsApp routes end-to-end encrypted content and processes account, phone, device, connection and usage metadata; the cited policy does not establish that the server never holds content keys.
Hunted for evidence a stolen unlocked phone exposes every app; Apple documents passcode-theft risk and Stolen Device Protection, not universal exposure.
Physical device: Stolen unlocked phone exposes all logged-in apps
Stolen unlocked phone can expose logged-in apps; exposure depends on lock state and app protections.
Hunted for evidence push bombing is not a real technique; MITRE documents MFA request generation and fatigue.
Hunted for evidence 0ktapus stole session cookies; Group-IB documents credential and 2FA-code capture, not session-cookie theft.
The 2022 0ktapus campaign used reverse-proxy phishing to steal session cookies and bypass MFA across thousands of accounts, showing that token theft is often easier than breaking TLS.
The 2022 0ktapus campaign used reverse-proxy phishing to capture credentials and MFA codes across thousands of accounts; the cited source does not establish session-cookie theft.

Android accessibility: Banking trojan reads screen, captures OTP, taps confirm
Android accessibility services can read window content and perform gestures; a specific banking trojan using that capability is a threat-report claim, not established by the platform reference.
Platform capability confirmed; trojan specific narrowed.

Android overlay: Tapjacking / fake interface over a banking app
Android provides obscured-touch filtering because overlays can obscure taps; a specific tapjacking chain against a banking app is not established here.
Hunted for evidence Android cannot install non-Play apps; Android documents installing apps from other sources, subject to permissions. Specific malicious APK not in source.
Android sideloading: Malicious APK or dropper
Android can install apps from sources other than Play, subject to user permission; a specific malicious APK/dropper is not established by the help page.
Installation path supported; malware specific narrowed.
Hunted for evidence MDM cannot manage devices; Apple documents MDM enrollment and configuration profiles. Malicious use requires enrollment/consent or supervision.
iOS configuration: Malicious profile or MDM enrollment enables interception/management
MDM enrollment and configuration profiles can manage devices; malicious use depends on enrollment/consent or supervision, not a universal interception path.
Management capability confirmed; malicious path conditional.
Hunted for evidence iCloud account access cannot expose synced data; Apple documents iCloud data/backup categories and E2EE options. Takeover requires account compromise.
Apple account: iCloud account takeover exposes synced data and backups
iCloud account takeover can expose synced data and backups, depending on the data category, backup encryption and account recovery state.
Hunted for evidence USB Restricted Mode is absolute; Apple documents the lockout, while research has reported bypasses. The cited page does not establish a working bypass.
iOS physical: USB Restricted Mode bypass on a locked device
USB Restricted Mode limits USB data access on a locked device; bypasses have been reported in research, but a working bypass is not established by the cited page.
Hunted for evidence consumer AI tools do not collect user content; OpenAI documents collection of prompts, files and account data. Exposure depends on settings/retention.
AI assistant: Sensitive data pasted into a consumer AI tool
Consumer AI tools may collect prompts and uploaded content under their privacy policy; exposure depends on account settings, retention and feature use.
Hunted for evidence approvals cannot move tokens; the ERC-20 approve/allowance/transferFrom flow lets a spender move approved tokens. A malicious approval can therefore drain the approved amount.
Crypto approvals: Malicious approve/permit drains tokens
ERC-20 approvals let a spender move the approved token amount; a malicious approval can drain that approved balance, but not necessarily the whole wallet.
Drain scope narrowed to approved amount.
Hunted for evidence address poisoning/clipboard hijacking is not a documented scam; Ethereum security guidance documents address spoofing/phishing risks. Exact clipboard chain not in fetched page.
Crypto addresses: Address poisoning or clipboard hijacking
Address poisoning and clipboard hijacking are documented crypto scam patterns; a specific clipboard chain is not established by the cited page.
Hunted for evidence a seed phrase does not control wallet recovery; Ethereum states the seed phrase is the only way to recover the wallet and must be kept offline.
Hunted for evidence bridge exploits do not drain funds; Chainalysis documents bridge hacks as major fund drains. Not every bridge/contract is exploitable.
Crypto bridge/contract: Protocol exploit drains funds
Bridge and contract exploits can drain funds; exploitability is protocol-specific, not a universal property of bridges.
Hunted for evidence deepfakes cannot authorize transfers; FBI documents deepfake/social-engineering transfer fraud. A specific transfer requires victim action.
Deepfake / social engineering: Synthetic video or voice authorises a transfer
Synthetic video/voice can support social-engineering transfer fraud; the transfer still requires victim authorization, and deepfakes are not the only route.

Hunted for evidence DNS control cannot redirect traffic; CISA documents DNS infrastructure tampering and illegitimate DNS activity. The page does not establish timing analysis or every look-alike outcome.
Whoever controls name resolution can decide whether a bank, update server or password-reset link resolves to the real service or a look-alike, and can block or time connections.
Control of name resolution can redirect or block resolution and support look-alike routing; timing analysis and every outcome are not established by the cited CISA page.
